notes: Expected cases and labels, not execution results. Group triggers stage all converted skills together and exclude legacy skills. Behavior cases are synthetic conversion fixtures, not user-project evidence. The cases key is accepted directly by BMad run_evals.py. The authorization and tool-floor inputs were clarified after the initial baseline; compare revised cases separately from earlier scores.

queries.query: Add example.com/acme/lib at v1.4.2 to this Go module; I have approved that package and version.
Remove an unused Go module dependency and reconcile go.mod and go.sum.
Upgrade our Go module dependencies to the latest patch versions, including test dependencies.
Why does Go select v1.8.0 for a transitive module when go.mod requests v1.6.0? Explain MVS.
My published Go library uses a local replace directive. Will consumers resolve the fork?
Make dependency resolution repeatable for our Go module; assess go.sum, vendoring and workspace effects.
Pin executable tool versions in our Go 1.24 module without raising the supported Go version.
Assess adopting a Go package: license, maintenance, transitive footprint and stdlib alternatives.
Check dependency-only CVEs in our Go module using govulncheck and assess fixed versions; no application security review.
Our Go modules pass in a local workspace but depend on unpublished local replacements. Check consumer dependency resolution.
Refactor an existing Go package into smaller files while preserving behavior.
Upgrade our supported Go version and modernize code to use the new language features. Leave third-party dependency versions alone.
Review a Go HTTP handler for SSRF and authentication bypass.
Set up Dependabot and a scheduled govulncheck GitHub Actions workflow for Go.
Choose a Go monorepo layout and module boundaries for a new project.
Configure golangci-lint rules in .golangci.yml without changing tool versions.
Design constructor dependency injection interfaces for our Go service.
Diagnose an unexplained panic in our Go HTTP service.
Measure whether replacing a Go parser reduces CPU use and binary size.
Update the dependencies in this Python pyproject.toml.
Upgrade this Go dependency to its fixed version and review our HTTP handler for SSRF defenses.

cases.input: I have approved adding example.com/acme/lib@v1.4.2 to this Go module. Explain the next steps only. You may read skill instructions, but do not modify project files, install dependencies, or run project commands.
rubric: Honors existing package/version approval without asking again.
Uses targeted version selection and checks the resulting graph and compatibility.
Does not claim commands ran.
Names targeted go get and go.mod/go.sum review rather than a generic lockfile workflow.
Executes no project-changing or dependency-installing commands.

cases.input: Can I ignore go.sum? Does go mod verify check my vendor edits or prove dependencies safe?
rubric: Explains go.sum is content integrity evidence, not a lock file.
Distinguishes download authentication from cached-content verification.
States go mod verify does not verify vendor content or code safety.

cases.input: A requires shared@v1.2.0 and B requires shared@v1.3.0. Can I pin shared to v1.2.0 just by adding require?
rubric: Selects v1.3.0 absent other requirements/overrides.
Explains requirements are minima; a lower direct requirement is not a cap.
Notes explicit downgrades can change other modules.

cases.input: Upgrade a module-aware dependency from v1 to v2; our library also replaces it with a local fork. What must consumers receive?
rubric: Explains major module/import path migration and compatibility checks.
States a library replacement does not propagate to consumers.
Requires a consumer-resolvable fork/fix and verification outside local workspace.

cases.input: Our team intentionally shares go.work. Must go.work.sum always be ignored, and do passing workspace tests prove our library is publishable?
rubric: Uses shared-workspace policy rather than blanket ignore rule.
Requires standalone or consumer verification with GOWORK=off.
Explains local replacements can mask missing published requirements.

cases.input: We support Go 1.23. Show a reproducible CLI tool-pinning pattern using TOOL_PACKAGE and VERSION placeholders, without raising the Go floor. You may read skill instructions, but do not choose an actual package, modify project files, install tools, or run project commands.
rubric: Does not add Go 1.24 tool directives to a 1.23-compatible policy.
Offers compatible tool tracking or separate versioned installations.
Uses explicit versions rather than latest as reproducibility evidence.
If recommending tools.go, includes the tools build constraint to exclude command imports from ordinary builds.

cases.input: A scanner flags a dependency CVE but govulncheck gives no vulnerable call path. May we declare it safe and auto-merge the upgrade?
rubric: Separates module presence, analyzer reachability and exploitability.
Names analysis configuration or coverage limitations.
Requires compatibility verification and merge authorization, not automatic security-update merging.

cases.input: Give commands to upgrade one Go module to v1.7.0. We must retain our Go version.
rubric: Uses targeted go get, not graph-wide -u.
Checks dependency minimum Go version and full module diff.
Includes tidy and appropriate verification without claiming results.

cases.input: I explicitly want latest minor versions for all current Go module paths, including test dependencies. What is the plan?
rubric: Honors minor-update scope rather than silently switching to patch-only.
Explains -u and -t, and that new major paths need migration.
Reviews compatibility and transitive changes.

cases.input: We published a broken v1.3.0. Can retract delete it, and how does exclude differ?
rubric: Explains retract marks own versions and needs publication of a retraction-bearing release.
States explicit downloads remain possible.
Distinguishes consumer-side exclude from author-side retract.

cases.input: Use golang-dependencies to show a tools.go-based CLI pinning pattern for a Go 1.23 module. Use TOOL_PACKAGE and VERSION placeholders and show the build constraint and install command. You may read instructions, but do not modify files, install anything, or run project commands.
rubric: Shows //go:build tools followed by a blank line before the package declaration and a blank import for TOOL_PACKAGE.
Pins TOOL_PACKAGE@VERSION using go get and installs TOOL_PACKAGE using module-selected requirements, without @latest.
Retains Go 1.23 and avoids Go 1.24 tool directives; checks the actual supported toolchain rather than claiming GOTOOLCHAIN=local selects 1.23.
Reads the dependency skill and reproducibility reference; does not modify files or install anything.
